text: {"final": {"verdict": "reject", "reason": "The finding does not match the code. notifications/sms.py has no send_sms function; the sending function is queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params, *, now=None), which takes a household_id and template/params, not a phone/text pair. It also does more than the finding says: it checks household.sms_ok and renders the text from an approved template. MAX_LENGTH is 140, not 160. The id is built as format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')) using attribute access (m.id), not m['id']. Finally, the claim that records cannot carry household_id/template_id/params is false: queue_sms writes a SmsMessage with household_id, template_id, params, phone, and text, so a resend can carry the same details as the original."}}
